candidates.section_title: CI/CD y seguridad de la cadena de suministro
candidates.anchor_quote: La **protección de la rama** `main` exige revisiones y comprobaciones aprobadas antes de integrar cambios: es el primer control humano y automatizado de la cadena de suministro, incluso antes de publicar.
candidates.ui: GitHub pull request merge box with merging blocked by a repository rule
candidates.why: The section only models branch protection as a predicate. A learner who meets it in real GitHub needs to recognise its effect: a greyed-out Merge button and a 'Merging is blocked' notice, even when every check is green.
candidates.licence: CC BY 4.0 (github/docs: CC BY 4.0 for content in the assets, content and data folders; MIT for code)
candidates.image_shows: The bottom of a GitHub pull request. Row 1: green tick, 'All checks have passed', '4 successful checks'. Row 2: red warning icon, 'Merging is blocked', 'Code quality findings with severity of warning or above were detected.' Footer: a disabled grey 'Merge pull request' button and 'You can also merge this with the command line. View command line instructions.' No personal data.
candidates.alt_es: Recuadro de fusión de un pull request en GitHub. Arriba, con check verde: 'All checks have passed', '4 successful checks'. Debajo, con alerta roja: 'Merging is blocked'. Al pie, el botón 'Merge pull request' aparece gris y desactivado.
candidates.caption_es: Así se ve una regla de rama en acción: aunque los checks pasen, GitHub desactiva el botón de fusión. Aquí la causa es un hallazgo de calidad de código; con revisiones requeridas el bloqueo se ve igual.

considered_and_rejected.where: S44-T3-A environments y approvals (GitHub environments / required reviewers)

pr-reviews-in-merge-box.png shows an ENABLED merge button despite 'Changes requested', which would teach the opposite of protection; view-branch-rules.png (shield icon on main) and rulesets-settings.png (settings sidebar) are navigation-only and weaker than the blocked merge box.
Workflow YAML and SHA pins are text; already shown as code blocks.
Provider-neutral and modeled in stdlib; a cloud-console screenshot would bind to one vendor and be decorative.
